text.content:
An old shearing station, cold now - iron clamps and a foot-pump bellows sit disused beside a grate still faintly warm to the touch. Drifts of wool, some clean, most not, have piled ankle-deep in the corners.

GM Notes

Breather: No active hazard. This was clearly a working danger once - the equipment is real, not decorative - but nobody's used it recently.

Subquest - The Shearing Pit: A search of the wool drifts (or a simple description offer) turns up a young, badly-matted llama that wandered in and got stuck fast in the accumulated fleece. Freeing and shearing it properly is a five-minute distraction with no combat attached, and leaves the party with a sack of good wool - worth a little coin, or worth nothing except a grateful llama, depending how mercenary the table wants to be.
